title: The therapeutic role of Coccinia grandis in flavor-enhancing high-lipid diet-induced chronic kidney disease: a dual role of NF-kB and TGF-beta/smad in renal fibrosis.
authors: Banerjee, Arnab; Roy, Jayati; Sarkar, Diptendu; Shil, Aparna; Das, Debasmita; Seal, Tapan; Mukherjee, Sandip; Maji, Bithin Kumar
one_liner_zh: 该文研究植物提取物对高脂饮食诱导慢性肾病的保护作用，涉及NF-kB和TGF-beta通路及分子对接，但核心是疾病治疗而非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，仅分子对接为边缘方法。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Coccinia grandis (CG), a plant used as traditional medicine, possesses antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-fibrotic activities. Chronic kidney disease (CKD) and renal fibrosis are public health issues, further promoted by monosodium glutamate in high-lipid diets (MH) via oxidative stress and inflammation. CG could potentially alleviate MH-induced CKD by modulating cell signaling. The purpose of this study is to hypothesize that CG, with known anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, might counteract MH-induced kidney dysfunction through its putative modulation of the signaling pathway. METHODS AND RESULTS: Male Wistar rats were administered ethanol extracts of CG leaves (etCGL) with or without MH for 28 days, and their effects on renal homeostasis, inflammation, and fibrosis were assessed. Finally, the major components of the MH and CG were docked to identify a better docking affinity and a stable interaction of the ligand with its receptor, highlighting the therapeutic target specificity. etCGL effectively improved kidney function, prevented oxidative stress, and decreased pro-inflammatory cytokines (TGF-beta, collagen) in rats fed with MH. Histology demonstrated restored renal structure and minimal fibrosis in the MH + etCGL-fed group. The renoprotective activities of etCGL with its phytocompounds such as catechin, p-coumaric acid, and naringenin as a composite extract were mediated by inhibiting NF-kB and TGF-beta/Smad pathways. CONCLUSIONS: Therefore, it can be concluded that CG, with its active compounds, can be a useful dietary approach in MH-associated CKD. Clinical trials across populations would establish the efficacy of etCGL, and understanding its molecular mechanism will be crucial for elucidating the mechanisms of its protective action.
abstract_zh: 背景：Coccinia grandis (CG) 是一种用作传统药物的植物，具有抗氧化、抗炎和抗纤维化活性。慢性肾脏病（CKD）和肾纤维化是公共卫生问题，高脂饮食中的谷氨酸钠（MH）通过氧化应激和炎症进一步促进其发展。CG可能通过调节细胞信号传导来缓解MH诱导的CKD。本研究的目的是假设CG凭借其已知的抗炎和抗氧化特性，可能通过其对信号通路的推定调节作用来对抗MH诱导的肾功能障碍。方法与结果：雄性Wistar大鼠接受CG叶片乙醇提取物（etCGL）联合或不联合MH处理28天，评估其对肾脏稳态、炎症和纤维化的影响。最后，将MH和CG的主要成分进行对接，以确定配体与其受体之间更好的对接亲和力和稳定相互作用，突出治疗靶点的特异性。etCGL有效改善了肾功能，预防了氧化应激，并降低了MH喂养大鼠中的促炎细胞因子（TGF-beta、胶原蛋白）。组织学显示，MH + etCGL喂养组肾结构恢复，纤维化最小。etCGL及其植物化合物（如儿茶素、对香豆酸和柚皮素）作为复合提取物的肾脏保护活性是通过抑制NF-kB和TGF-beta/Smad通路介导的。结论：因此，可以得出结论，CG及其活性化合物可作为MH相关CKD的有用饮食方法。跨人群的临床试验将确立etCGL的疗效，理解其分子机制对于阐明其保护作用机制至关重要。
